30272: Barenka's priests care nothing for mortal affairs—not Taxes nor wars. Hunting heretics, crushing cults, and sacrificing to ancestral Deitys matter more. Yet Normal residents fare no better here. Priest spies blanket the city, masters of exaggeration, distortion, and false accusation.
30273: Rich in plump lambs and water, Sanjar is Sasin's wealthiest Area. Its rulers—princes of great Familys—thus scheme endlessly against the crown, drowning in power struggles with time on their hands.
30274: None know where these vengeful spirits come from or where they go, but their piercing screams make one thing clear: they're no friendly company.
30275: Enduring thirst and hunger, these desperados hide among the desert mountains. Most bandits were once slaves themselves, yet now engage in slave trading to survive.
30276: Once a bustling City, now a desolate ruin. Falati fell in the Third Dynasty's war with the Forest Elves after Bovark Viceroy destroyed a home tree, prompting the Forest Elves to turn it to rubble. Now, only Lostlight Society researchers venture into the ancient city.
30277: Ghulam's Commanders coveted the pristine waters upstream of Puta, Farah's mother river. They hired master brewers from Caucaid and Chen-Yuan at great expense. After years of effort, they finally satisfy their fleeting cravings.
30278: In Kamara Port at Farah's northeast corner, pirate lords and Fallen Elves admirals frequent its shadow harbor. Beneath swirling currents, they trade interests from their domains - though clashes erupt when profits divide unevenly.
30279: Slavers from Lipanni sorely underestimated captives' thirst for freedom. They could learn much about "handling merchandise" from their predecessors - the slave masters of Monkos.
30280: When Fasut's princes developed a taste for stimulating olive-oil drinks, Atia's landlords forced farmers to surrender fields, burning wheat to plant elven olive trees - thus Olive Manor was born.
30281: As one of Atia's few surviving estates, Aleyn endured the landlords' tyranny through premium wheat and Friendly ties with Ghulam's Commanders... But Fasut's princes won't forget this insult. Retribution will come.
30282: War is everywhere, and ever shall be. No true beginning, no final end... The world itself is war - an unceasing struggle. —King Kurulek
30283: As Sasin's rare inland port, Lit holds an awkward position in Bovark Province. Merchants must carefully appease Fasut's princes, manage relations with Farah's Viceroy, and endure relentless extortion from river pirates along Puta's banks.
30284: In Bato culture, camels symbolize loyalty and endurance. Legend says these virtues dwell in their dual humps - drink camel milk to receive ancestral Deity's blessing and become a mighty Warrior.
30285: The Lipanni people ultimately have their standards—they didn't build the slave Marketplace within their city walls but chose a remote spot, feigning ignorance. As the Chen-Yuan people say: "What the eye doesn't see, the heart doesn't grieve over."
30286: Young Lipanni survive the sandstorms thanks to ancestral Deity blessings and this newly discovered vein... To honor its gift, they sought a grand name, yet debates dragged on without resolution.
30287: Slaves who couldn't walk or disobeyed were often chained to lakeside trees by traders, "granted freedom"... Over time, crocodiles thrived here. For easy remembrance, Lipanni dubbed it Crocodile Lake—where HP cycles.
30288: Ghulam's Commanders often joke they're royal exiles—their "soldiers" mere criminals, prisoners, and slaves seeking redemption... Once a dark humor, now at PRECARIOUS EDGE, it feels chillingly real.
30289: To prevent minor clashes from escalating, Farah's Viceroy meets Fasut princes here regularly... Talks always end sour, but still beat bloody battlefield duels.
30290: Whoever claims Fahler Castle must choose: side with Farah's Viceroy, bow to Fasut's princes, or watch tigers fight?
30291: As Fasut's henchmen, Delia tribes are feared across Sasin. Cross a prince in Bawak? You might survive. Cross these Delia brutes? Pray friends collect your family's corpses.
30292: Sea Gate Castle houses the royal guard. They enforce loyalty to Bato's King among Bawak's factions, while keeping neighbor Gro in check—lest they dream up another doomed war.
30293: Atia, Bawak's most fertile Area with crystal-clear oases, should want for nothing. Yet "Gegeluoye"—Bato's famine demon—haunts this land, reaping souls on schedule.
30294: Since Lipanni's founding, Udaya's princes never deigned to acknowledge these upstarts. Slave trade? Ore deals? Not "proper." Only scheming and rebellion are worthy pursuits.
30295: Outwardly, Uligan's priests cooperate with Lipanni for profit. Privately, the high priest schemes... When timing's ripe, he'll expose Lipanni's evils and gift slaves a "taste of freedom."
30296: During the "War of the Royal Heirs" between Gro and Bato, the Farah princes of Sasin descent backed Bato—a fatal misstep. None were pardoned. Yet Farah endures, its people crying out for a ruler. The Crown sent loyalists as interim frontier Viceroys, awaiting a resolution... To this day, none came, and "interim" was later scrapped.
30297: Fasut—a lucky upstart after the war—was once a humble fishing village. Farah princes exiled for opposing Bato hid in Puta's coastal Fisherman's Village, dubbing it "Fasut" ("truly noble" in Ancient Empire). They killed their kin but lost the Crown's trust. Now they huddle across the river, dreaming of Farah.
30298: As Sasin's youngest City, Lipanni is an afterthought—no history, no noble blood. Monkos slavers' charity let it cling to Bowak. Still, its immigrants bet this new home will one day stun the Sasin dynasty.
30299: Brutes here extort slave camps but hail passing slavers as "brothers," sharing spring water.
30300: Slavers dump worthless slaves in Crocodile Lake—or the Cobra Cave, a top disposal spot. Guards even stand by to assist.
30301: On The End's land, a twisted "forest" grows. Amid tangled, writhing tentacles, a Ancient Empire ruin seems buried in flesh and blood, but all paths are blocked by tentacles.
30302: Ruins of an Ancient EmpireCity littered with shattered idols—each face gouged out. Waves of negative emotions unsettle you, yet signs of habitation persist even here
30303: This grove defies expectations: no vitality, only the stench of decay. Its trees feel like withered skin, oozing pus-like sap
30304: Though most Grimspawn crave power and intrigue, rare ascetics abandon worldly desires. They endure trials to reach this altar of seekers—only to wield newfound power for greater schemes
30305: Low-grade stone from this quarry barely serves Construction. Yet the Cruelkin Dispatch masses of slaves here, graciously promising freedom if they build an eight-tiered spire with this rock
30306: Aliens, POWs, dissidents, and fallen rivals—all discarded into this junkyard as slaves-to-be. No guards patrol, but specially-crafted shackles suffocate prisoners nearing the outer walls
30308: A solitary tower that once rivaled the Twin Spires, it ultimately collapsed into ruins amid endless infighting. Its top floor was destroyed as punishment for the defeated, while rumors and eerie tales shroud the remnants—even scavengers dare not set foot.
30309: Since breaking free from Outer Deity's enslavement, Demonspawn no longer rely on "Bone Stitchers" for healing. Yet they maintain a small camp where these artisans occasionally receive unusual commissions—mostly unrelated to medicine
30310: For the Cruelkin, a dying creature's final wail is the finest nectar. They greedily savor this delicacy in execution grounds, battlefields, and arenas. Legends say the best Elosé wine must contain this essence
30311: Some Cruelkin devoted to The Arcane Dome survived the ancient purge. They now hide within Ancient Battlefield ruins, awaiting the prophesied "Chosen One"
30312: Some demons surviving Black Peaks' power struggles come to this leaning spire. Along with "idealists" opposing the Peaks' rule, they plot conspiracies to seize power.
30313: Twisted tentacles writhe everywhere. This is the Spire of Soul Shaper, stronghold of Violet Eye Believer. The notoriously cruel Black Peaks tolerates these fanatics not by granting them paradise to spread their gospel, but because it lacks means to eradicate them.
30314: Countless jagged peaks and stone towers pierce the sky, challenging divine authority—this is Black Peaks, breeding ground of death and conspiracy. Every moment, bodies plummet from summits, impaled on stone forests or smashed into pulp. Even the steel-hearted shudder at such sights, yet locals remain unfazed. Young demons scavenge corpses while elders watch from afar, awaiting opportunities to steal spoils—this is Black Peaks, breeding ground of death and conspiracy.
30315: O King, you dreamed of a Violet Eye giant—towering, cloaked in violet light. All your subjects turned to worship Him. —「Book of Mercy」31:2
30316: Whoever among you claims kingship shall reign for millennia; whoever betrays shall enslave billions. As the Violet Eye Lord declared: He came not to serve fools, but to make fools serve God. —「Book of Mercy」28:20
30317: Under Violet Eye's gaze, the Watcher turns bronze to gold, iron to silver, peace to warfire, justice to dung. —「Book of Mercy」17:60
30318: My Lord named Eden the Valley of Slaughter, for war shall ravage it. Corpses will pile into mountains, blood flow into lakes, while my Lord walks amidst, bringing violet light to reign over carnage. —「Book of Mercy」6:19
30319: Between us, The End sets boundaries. For one as righteous as you to escape this inferno, kissing the feet of God and converting to worship Violet Eye is impossible. Just as my betrayal of the Lord, falling from this paradise into hell to revel in torment, is equally impossible. —「Book of Mercy」26:16
30320: Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I fear no evil; for the Lord is with me. His violet radiance shines upon me, Knock Backing The Silence, driving death away. —「Book of Mercy」4:23
30321: Death may be thy salvation, yet the Sovereign shall cast violet light to resurrect thee, commit six hundred sixty-six sins of Desecrate, then execute thee for apostasy—true death.—The Merciful Scriptures 14:16
30322: Even the savage clan of chaotic Desecrate cannot tolerate Violet Eye Believer... As precaution, they erected sky-piercing watchtowers beyond the secret forest where the Violet Eye god slumbers, ever vigilant against Nothingness's movements.
30323: These watchtowers, meant to surveil Violet Eye Believer, now stand corrupted in service to the God of Nothingness. The twisted tentacles sprawling around them are grim testament to this.
30324: Fallen Leaf Grounds, Springland's grandest arena of life-and-death duels. Witness to knights' glory and chivalry, it's also where destinies of Springen, Mynan, and Berchmon entwine—their final battlefield.
30325: Swearing upon silver lances, the Feline ancestors vowed to remain the sharp blade within Springen's crest. As a renowned knightly Family, their fortress hosts trials for Wildland Knight aspirants.
30326: Springland's affairs draw only cold indifference from Northnode's Mage—be it knights' heroic legends or traitors' schemes. They shun politics, yet this remains but a wistful dream.
30327: As Springland's vital port on the Nansai River, Springport welcomes merchant fleets bearing ore and components upstream. Departing vessels brim with Wildland wines, sailing downstream toward homecoming glory.
30328: Baron Mord of Vine Lake Manor lost his ancestral castle in an uprising thirty years past. Finding the manor serene and fragrant, he and his heirs remain in no rush to reclaim their birthright.
30329: Five decades ago, Springen Farm bore the name Paris Estate. Its baron's impatience proved his undoing—revealing his treachery too soon, drawing Springen's wrath and forfeiting these lands.
30330: To curry the archbishop's favor, Mynan's marquis overruled objections, renaming Delis Mine as Sunset Mine. All its yield now flows unreservedly to The Rising Church, seeking absolution for his The Sins.
30331: Although the Mynan's Campbell family may not devoutly worship any single Deity, they strive to appease every religion. The grand temple of The Rising, the lush foliage of The Grow shrine, and the baptism traditions of Dew Believer all coexist within their singular chapel.
30332: Peasants at Harvey's Winery might be the happiest subjects in Springland, since Baron Harvey neglects governance, obsessively hunts year-round in Sinus Forest west of Lumber Mill, and sometimes even forgets to collect taxes when having too much fun
30333: Once property of House Spring, now managed by Lady Aval. Its grapes and wines rank top-notch in Springland and throughout Caucaid. The legendary Knights Fertileland also embarked on their journeys nourished by these very vineyards
30334: As one of Berchmon's few reputable Mercenary orders, Grandiflora Brigade secretly contracted with Vineyard Haven, bypassing Marquis Springen. Though few know the details, banditry around the vineyards has drastically decreased
30335: Resembling a military encampment more than a farmstead. Marquis Berchmon, coveting the vineyards' profits across the river, stationed troops here - ready to seize this lucrative prize when opportunity strikes
30336: Councillors of Lorik Autonomous Region prefer holding meetings at Sanbai Institute outside city walls. For these freedom-seekers, knight-ruled Lorik still feels suffocating at times, while Sanbai Institute - birthplace of their liberation - offers homely comfort
30337: Crossroad Mercenary Group evolved from highwaymen, mountain bandits, and wandering Martial Artists across Caucaid. These Thugs drifted near Loir Valley until Marquis Berchmon recruited them, transforming the rabble into knights tasked with safeguarding Berchmon
30338: Yè Merchant Guild's headquarters lies hidden in deep woods, devoid of splendor. The merchants know they may shine elsewhere, but in Springland, they must play second fiddle to the knights on center stage
30339: With Berchmon Marquisate's approval, Baron Paris established a new lumber estate northeast of Berchmon. Marquis Springen fumed impotently - times had changed and things were no longer as before
30340: Though Lorik Autonomous Region won't meddle in knights' honor games, its councilors run the "Gold Buying Club" betting ring outside arenas to fuel rivalries.
30341: Faded inscriptions cover this crumbling stone stele... Elders say it tells of Springland's first Duke and their timeless feud with Steelland.
30343: Marquis Berchmon's Outpost Mission secures the border while recruiting promising rebels/bandits into his knightly forces.
30344: Baron Paris and Aragon ignore this derelict Lumber Mill, letting it become Springland's lawless corner.
30345: Officially guarding Aragon Fishing Village from Fallen Elves pirates for Marquis Berchmon, the Fire Emblem Outpost Mercenary knights secretly watch Baron Aragon.
30346: Without coastal Fallen Elves pirates, Aragon fishermen prosper—thanks to Marquis Berchmon's tax cuts and Baron Aragon's benevolence.
30347: Campbell house claimed Hubard Family's castle as Knights Hound's base after their exile. Nobles call it "Pizarro's Kennel"—a joke commoners avoid.
30348: Before The Rising faith reigned, Springland worshipped the Lady of the Lake. Legends say she watches knights through these waters, guiding them to triumph or ruin after granting seven chivalric virtues.
30349: Baron Madden depends on cross-border trade unlike other Springland knights. Marquis Berchmon's reforms thus tempt him to disloyalty.
30350: Baron Harvey would rather be a Hunter than endure knighthood's politics. Fate nonetheless gave him his father's title and sword.
30351: Baron Thar follows The Rising but less zealously than liege Marquis Mynan. He weighs pledging loyalty to Springen or Berchmon for his family's sake.
30352: Thirty-five years ago, when Mynan Marquis took over from his father, Baron Plazet launched an earth-shattering rebellion. Few know how, but the result speaks for itself—Plazet barony renamed New Dawn Harbor, gifted by the current Mynan Marquis to the bishop.
30353: The Paris family has always been weather-vane, clear from the fox emblem on their crest. Ironically, loyalty-lacking, they've scraped by through crisis after crisis, becoming one branch of Springland's ancient knight Family…
30354: Breaking Springland's knight traditions, the current Baron Luwa took over a distant cousin's role with Marquis Berchmon's tacit consent… Simply put, a warlord backed by Berchmon family forcibly usurped the Luwa baron title.
30355: Baron Golu began as a minor clerk—no other skills, but top-notch at taxes and loans. That won him Marquis Berchmon's eye. In a moment of emotion, finding a wise lord, Golu poisoned his master as a dark gift to Berchmon. Moved to tears, Marquis Berchmon gave Golu the vacant baron title, making him the current Baron Golu.
30356: Aragon family has ancient roots, tracing back to Kingdom Helton. Thus, they cherish knight traditions, and the current Baron Aragon is a true knight sworn to guard goddess virtues.
30357: Birthplace of House Spring, an integral part of Springland's history. Few families bond so tightly with their land. No matter how many City rise in Springland, Springen holds special meaning.
30358: A coastal City famed for trade, ancestral home of House Campbell. Thanks to sea routes and the Golden Road, Mynan grew from a town to a major City in a decade. A strong commercial vibe permeates its streets; tradition, religion, and glory all fade before Ducat's glow.
30359: Berchmon City is vast with dense Construction, but its streets lack life. After the lords of House Aurelian were expelled, the City endured long blockades and plunder. Those scars linger on its body, forever marking the atrocities.
30360: This Fortress City guards Springland's western border, built by House Reimond, renowned from the Thorn War. During the war, faith in The Rising gave Reimond's army the courage to never retreat, and it became the primary faith across Lorraine. In Springland, which follows The Grow, Lorraine is the key stronghold for the The Rising sect.
30361: Knights disillusioned with their lord united to overthrow Baron Mord's rule. But lacking plans for what followed, they soon descended into infighting and betrayal... To this day, the Mord rebels remain in disarray.
30362: Knights opposing the Marquis of Mynan were driven into Springland's northeastern mountains—a perpetually cold, damp wasteland where even firewood is scarce... So they cast aside honor, becoming bandits who pilfer firewood.
30363: Even sharp informants can't count these outlaws' backers: Sanbai Institute? Berchmon Marquis? Or Mynan's bishop?
30364: Berchmon Marquis turns a blind eye to these mountain bandits, showing them more leniency than his own subjects—if they avoid his red line.
30365: Rumors say Berchmon's true heir survived, hiding in a Springland rebel manor and biding his time for vengeance.
30366: When the Fallen Elves ark fleet terrorized the seas, they built a sturdy fortress here. After the fleet fell, it became a base for Ark of Instinct Moon Pirate.
30367: Blinding magma churns nearby; scorched earth races into a devouring abyss—the Cave of Scorched Earth, sanctum of the gods' lastborn.
30368: Merciful Violet Eye sovereign, recalling old bonds, carved "Last Child's Window" for the rebel lastborn—jailed under endless magma in fiery torment per the "Merciful Canon"—to watch mortal strife.
30369: On pitch-black soil, a dark mountain looms over magma rivers, whispering tales of Kurulek King's Golden Age.
30370: After Bloodboiler Temple burned ancient Aktur, fire-diviners shipped "unworthy" souls to Cave of Proof. What must be proven? None know or care.
30371: Even brash flame warlords keep Brunning Suebowy clean. They stash plundered sacrifices here for pre-processing.
30372: Fire-masters coat fresh hides in rock salt, knead vigorously, then smoke with sacred fire—repeat until impenetrable. With leather armor obsolete, the Salt Mine lies abandoned.
30373: Flame-clan cowards face Desecrate at Iron Mask Monastery near Telted Ur'an—hands to crab claws, feet to ox hooves, faces under freshly forged steel masks.
30374: Telted Ur'an's sacred fire dies suddenly each year—lasting weeks or half a year. While it's out, The Seething priests use Molten Spring's hellfire to forge arms, hold rites, and sacrifice to their god without breaking vows.
30375: This land has drunk its fill of blood. Even amid molten flows, the soil stays damp. Rogue warbands clash here, settling disputes through deadly duels. Claim to be a warband? Prove your worth in the contest.
30376: Fun fact: Flame clan demons often get indigestion—demons gotta eat fast! To fix bellies, they gulp iron chunks, hoping to grind up bones inside.
30377: Lazy warlords or those feuding with Ur'an worship The Seething at nearby Fire Feeding Land. But these oafs skip steps or botch rituals. No blessings—only the Youngest Son's rage.
30378: Rumors say the Youngest Son's heart lies deep in the veins. Swallow it for godlike power. After centuries of digging, the Suebowy found no heart—just a Skullhunter nest. The mine was scrapped.
30379: Every high-reaching Suebowy warrior enters the Training Ground arena with their trusty Weapon, drums pounding. Survive? Earn a spot in the Warlord's Guard.
30380: Molten flows cool here, piling into pus-like flats from festering wounds. Scavengers dig up sunken treasures—sparking bloody brawls.
30381: Ancient Bloods believe death won't turn them into false gods' abominations. Their souls join the Father God on sacred battlefields. This tomb is for the fated. They armor up in splendor and march to their end. No one leaves.
30382: Aktur's survivors etched ancient truths on white steles for posterity. But heavenly fire swallowed the Area the moment they finished. 666 days later, it spat out charred rubble—the melted words lost to time.
30383: A giant stone coffin lies on the wasteland. Manuscripts, ancient texts, and seals pile high; white candles glow dimly. No one knows how long they've Burned. Rampaging Demonspawn avoid it, and devout The Rising followers only worship from afar.
30384: To prevent offerings' Escape and minimize losses, Subor warlords chain them to hall pillars, letting vultures pluck their eyes. Occasionally, a lucky one keeps a single eye... That's when the warlord steps in personally
30385: Bone Cutting Ground—the liveliest Marketplace in the Flame Tribe. Warlords from all corners brawl and bond here. Their underlings hustle to sell hunted offerings. When buyers show interest? Smash spines with clubs or sever limbs with cleavers—all for "premium service"
30386: The Treasure of the Heart doesn't hold living organs, but safeguards the secrets of the Subor demons. Yet its keeper isn't exactly tight-lipped—just offer a prime leg bone and it'll spill colossal secrets
30387: Subor warlords stay silent about past wars on these lands—especially the great battle against the Brutal Tribe. Normally, given their boastful Trait, they'd brag even about defeats. But here, they maintain Silence uncharacteristically
30388: Silver-tongued offerings get handpicked by The Seething priests. They're lavishly escorted to their final destination—Tongueless Inn. Turns out the priests fear the bored captive Youngest Child might call down heavenly fire, so they "gift" talkative talents to amuse it
30389: A charred scar on the wasteland, an ugly ossified remnant. Blazespawn rebels against the Sole Master built a City named Aktur, trying to spread false history. The Moltenblood Legion besieged, burned, and destroyed that City, but deep in its remains, some cling to old dreams, refusing to wake.
30390: No one knows how Subor was built. Some say it formed from the weathered bones of prey left by the Youngest; others claim The Seething seized the lair of the Primordial Magma Dragon and reshaped it with fists; still others insist it was created after Violet Eye's Lord made a bet with friends... In short, Subor's origins remain a mystery. Fortunately, its rulers—the uncultured demon warlords of various war gangs—care little about such things. They focus only on their territories, tomorrow's meals, and the next battle. Rumors say elven Scholars once disguised themselves as sacrificial offerings to investigate the truth of Brunning Suebowy, but most research ended at Tooth Extraction Ridge, Bone Cutting Ground, and the Broken Tongue Inn.
30391: The second City of Blazespawn, this massive fortress was built and controlled by the Moltenblood Legion. Only with Uhl'an could the Moltenblood Legion stand firm against Suebowy's Flameclaimers. Uhl'an's forges blaze ceaselessly, transmuting plundered spoils into heavy iron armor for Legion Warriors.
30392: The temperamental warlord of Rock Roar Warband often berates or beats subordinates on whims. Sometimes he forces captured sacrifices to howl at rocks, commanding underlings to dance to the sounds for amusement.
30393: Since unknown times, Violet Eye's Fanatical Believers congregated here... Suebowy's warlords raise no objections, occasionally "visiting" the camp to seize fresh sacrifices for quick snacks.
30394: The former leader of Ironfire Warband believed himself born of superheated black iron. To prove it, he screamed and leapt into a scalding molten iron pool... Thereafter, Ironfire Warband welcomed a new warlord.
30395: Warband cowards and traitors have ears/noses severed, limbs broken, and get dumped here... To prevent survivors, Suebowy's warlords even hired Shadow Guards to periodically purge the camp.
30396: The warlord of Evilfire Warband lost half his face to Uhl'an's sacred flame. Since then, fire terrifies him—only drowning himself in blood can briefly overcome this Fear.
